'''David Nikolaevich Klyshko''' (Давид Николаевич Клышко), (1929&mdash;2000) was a Russian [[physicist]] and [[professor]]. A highly regarded Physics professor at  [[Moscow State University]], was known for his imperative approach for [[Quantum Optics]] understanding. His most known contributions were in the field of [[quantum electronics]] and [[quantum information science]].

His Habilitation [[thesis]] on the topic of [[spontaneous parametric down-conversion]], "''Multi-quantum and multi-particle transitions in [[radio spectroscopy]] and [[quantum radiophysics]]''," was published in 1972. Upon release, the thesis was widely recognized as a breakthrough in multi-particle transitions.

Throughout the 1970s, Klyshko presented several more important theoretical contributions including the development of [[spontaneous parametric down-conversion]] theory, [[Quantum entanglement|entanglement]]-based [[quantum imaging]], nonlinear transformations in [[quantum optics]], and the [http://www.turpion.org/php/paper.phtml?journal_id=pu&paper_id=2730 advanced wave model] for describing correlations in [[photon]] [[Interference (wave propagation)|interference]] experiments.
